problem:
Consider the following initial value problem for the functions $y=y(x),z=z(x):$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=6x+2y+z,\, & y(1)=-1 \\ {z}^{′}=2x-y+z,\, & z(1)=3\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method.
What entries should be placed in the columns for $Δy$ and $Δz$ in the table below if the step size is $Δx=1?$

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ |  |  | {{field-1}} |  |  | {{field-2}} |

Therefore, $y(2)≈$
{{field-3}}
and $z(2)≈$
{{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=f(x,y,z),\, & y(a)=c, \\ {z}^{′}=g(x,y,z),\, & z(a)=d,\end{aligned}
$$

Euler's method approximates the solution by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation. More precisely, the increments on $y$ and $z$ are

$$
{\begin{aligned}Δy={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ Δz={z}^{′}\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

The new values are then given by ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and ${z}_{\text{new}}=z+Δz.$

First, because the initial conditions are $y(1)=-1$ and $z(1)=3,$ we place $y=-1$ and $z=3$ in the table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-1$ |  |  | $3$ |  |  |

Next, we compute both ${y}^{′}$ and ${z}^{′}$ according to the given rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =6x+2y+z \\  & =6\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+3 \\  & =6-2+3 \\  & =7 \\ {z}^{′} & =2x-y+z \\  & =2\cdot 1-(-1)+3 \\  & =2+1+3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-1$ | $7$ |  | $3$ | $6$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ and $Δz$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =7\cdot 1 \\  & =7, \\ Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =6\cdot 1 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-1$ | $7$ | $7$ | $3$ | $6$ | $6$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x,$ $Δy$ to $y,$ and $Δz$ to $z,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+1=2, \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=-1+7=6, \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=3+6=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-1$ | $7$ | $7$ | $3$ | $6$ | $6$ |
| $2$ | $6$ |  |  | $9$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈6$ and $z(2)≈9.$
